business_problem: Singapore Airlines wanted to improve customer support and travel discovery while giving employees governed AI tools for everyday work and software delivery.
solution_summary: Singapore Airlines uses the OpenAI API for customer-facing services and OpenAI models within Jarvis, its governed internal AI platform. The airline replaced Kris's scripted dialog flows with an LLM-powered chatbot that interprets natural-language intent, grounds answers in a knowledge base, handles multiple topics, and hands context to a human representative when needed. Flight Recommender combines an orchestration layer with fare and availability data to return natural-language travel suggestions. Customer-service representatives use API-powered call summaries, and engineering teams apply models across requirements, architecture review, testing, and production monitoring. Jarvis lets employees work with documents and create workflows in a controlled environment. Input/output validation, PII handling, authenticated access, and human review support responsible use across these deployments.

data_flow: Kris uses the OpenAI API and a knowledge base to answer customer questions; Flight Recommender combines customer intent with fare and availability data; Jarvis applies OpenAI models to employee documents and workflows, with validation and access controls around model inputs and outputs.

business_outcome: Singapore Airlines doubled customer satisfaction for Kris, reduced average handling time for representatives by about 10%, and grew Flight Recommender monthly users nearly threefold. Jarvis is used monthly by more than 60% of employees.
